output.headline: Hires Arntz Builders for $15.99M to build Claremont Middle School's multi-purpose room and kitchen
output.sourceIssueCandidate: The contract amount is printed as "$15, 985,725.00" with a stray space; it appears to mean $15,985,725.00.
output.summary: Arntz Builders, Inc. will construct a multi-purpose building and kitchen at Claremont Middle School. The contract was competitively bid and Arntz was the lowest responsive, responsible bidder. The amount includes a $1,300,000 contingency allowance, and work is expected to run about 434 days, from June 23, 2022 to August 31, 2023.

output.headline: Creates four new job descriptions and revises four others, including mental health and MTSS roles
output.summary: The board adopts a resolution creating four job descriptions: Program Manager for Mental Health Internships, Program Manager for McKinney Vento, Director of Multi-Tiered Systems of Support (MTSS), and Partner for MTSS. It also revises four existing descriptions, including Director Program Improvement and Director, Language Programs. No dollar amount is stated.

output.headline: Hires Redgwick Construction for $326,000 to replace play structure and matting at Madison Park Academy

money.evidence: in the lump sum amount of $326,000.00

output.summary: Redgwick Construction Company will remove the old play structure, repair the asphalt, and install a new play structure with Softiles rubber matting at Madison Park Academy. It was the lowest responsive, responsible bidder in a competitive bid. The lump sum includes a $12,000 contingency allowance, and the 90-day job is scheduled from June 23 to September 20, 2022.

output.headline: Extends the Escape Technology contract one year, up to $1,277,826.55, without competitive bidding
output.summary: The board finds the district can extend its existing Escape Technology, Inc. contract for one year (July 1, 2022 through June 30, 2023) without running a competitive bid. It also approves Addendum No. 5 with the Alameda County Office of Education for up to $1,277,826.55.

output.headline: Ratifies up to $6,880 for an arts program coordinator at Oakland Fine Arts Summer School
output.summary: The board ratifies an agreement with E.W. Wainwright to engage students in arts activities, coordinate assemblies and help the administrator run the Oakland Fine Arts Summer School, for up to $6,880.00. The agreement covers June 6 through July 8, 2022, and it began before the board's June 22 vote.

output.headline: Hires Arntz Builders for $14.17M to replace the Laurel Child Development Center
output.summary: Arntz Builders, Inc. will demolish the existing modular building and build a new single-story, roughly 7,400-square-foot building with five preschool classrooms, offices and a kitchen. It was the lowest responsible, responsive bidder in a competitive bid. The amount includes a $60,000 allowance for roof anchors and a $300,000 contingency, with work scheduled from June 23, 2022 to September 21, 2023.

output.headline: Ratifies Olson Remcho Law Firm for election and redistricting legal work, up to $95,000 a year

money.evidence: not to exceed $95,000 in a fiscal year

output.summary: The board ratifies a memorandum of understanding (MOU) and engagement policy that lets the Office of the General Counsel retain Olson Remcho Law Firm for legal work on redistricting, filling vacancies and other election matters, plus other legal services as needed. Pay is capped at $95,000 in a fiscal year. The agreement runs from March 1, 2022 through June 30, 2023, and it began before the board's vote.

output.headline: Applies for up to $82.4M from the state for the Community Schools Partnership Program through 2027
output.summary: The board approves the district's application to the California Department of Education for $82,394,086.00 in California Community Schools Partnership Program Implementation Grant funding. The money would support continuing and expanding Community Schools work district-wide from June 1, 2022 through June 30, 2027. The board also accepts the grant, in whole or in part, if it is awarded.

output.headline: Adds $20,000 and two months for a contractor managing the Expanded Learning Opportunities grant
output.summary: The board ratifies an amendment to a services agreement with Trina Fields, who provides project management and coordination for the Expanded Learning Opportunities Program grant. It adds 400 hours of work and $20,000.00, raising the cap from $30,000.00 to $50,000.00. It also extends the end date from June 30, 2022 to August 31, 2022.

output.headline: Pays Safe Passages up to $97,750 to coach Transitional Kindergarten-Kindergarten expanded learning programs
output.summary: The board approves a services agreement with Safe Passages for up to $97,750.00. Safe Passages will deliver a professional development series with technical assistance and coaching for school leaders at 37 Transitional Kindergarten-Kindergarten (TK/K) Expanded Learning lead agencies and their instructors. The goal is quality expanded learning for the district's youngest students from July 1, 2022 through June 30, 2023.

output.headline: Cuts $9,174.64 from Redgwick's Markham Elementary playmatting contract and extends it 94 days
output.summary: This change order credits the district for trellises that were delivered in error, lowering the contract with Redgwick Construction Company from $419,500.00 to $410,325.36. It also extends the contract by 94 days, from the earlier end date of November 23, 2021 to April 12, 2022. All other terms stay the same.

output.headline: Hires G & G Builders for $596,516 to replace play structure and matting at East Oakland Pride Elementary
output.summary: G & G Builders, Inc. will remove the old play structure, repair the asphalt, and install a new play structure with Softiles rubber matting at East Oakland Pride Elementary School. It was the lowest responsible, responsive bidder. The amount includes a $12,000 contingency allowance, and the 90-day job is scheduled from June 23 to September 20, 2022.

output.headline: Pays AGS up to $127,083 for geotechnical engineering review at McClymonds High School
output.summary: AGS, Inc. will provide geotechnical (soil and ground) and geohazard consulting, review data, manage sub-consultants and oversee contract administration for the McClymonds High School Modernization Project. The not-to-exceed amount includes up to $11,553 for additional services. Work runs from June 23, 2022 to July 31, 2025.

output.headline: Extends Jensen Hughes' fire and intrusion alarm design contract at MLK Jr. Elementary to June 2023
schools: Martin Luther King, Jr. Elementary School
output.summary: This amendment extends the term of Jensen Hughes' agreement for fire and intrusion alarm design and construction administration at Martin Luther King, Jr. Elementary School. The end date moves from May 31, 2022 to June 29, 2023, which is 394 more calendar days. No added money is stated, and all other terms stay the same.

output.headline: Pays ACC Environmental up to $7,826.50 to test soil for lead and arsenic at Burckhalter Elementary
output.summary: ACC Environmental Consultants, Inc. will test shallow soil for lead and arsenic and characterize soil waste before new athletic courts and a play structure are built at Burckhalter Elementary School. The not-to-exceed amount includes up to $711.50 for any additional services. Work runs from June 23, 2022 to June 23, 2023.

output.headline: Adds $198,000 and a year for Lowe Consulting's local-hiring and prevailing-wage monitoring
output.sourceIssueCandidate: The stated numbers do not add up: $588,000 plus the additional $198,000 is $786,000, but the text gives the new total as $756,000.
output.summary: This third amendment adds $198,000 to Lowe Consulting Group's contract for Project Labor Agreement services, which focus on hiring local residents and union representation and on monitoring prevailing wages and local apprentices. The text says the not-to-exceed amount goes from $588,000 to $756,000, and the term is extended 365 days, from June 30, 2022 to June 30, 2023. All other terms stay the same.

output.headline: Ratifies a no-cost summer camp and child care program by Adventure Time at Montclair Elementary
output.summary: The board ratifies a no-cost agreement with Adventure Time/Tuller Corporation to run its summer enrichment and child care program at Montclair Elementary School. The program ran from May 26 through July 31, 2022, and it began before the board's June 22 vote. It costs the district nothing.

output.headline: Pays Mayekawa USA up to $7,805 to inspect and train staff on a refrigeration system
output.sourceIssueCandidate: The project name is garbled: the title says "Cole Administration the Center Project" and the text says only "the Center Project". The vendor location is printed as "York, Philadelphia, PA".
output.summary: Mayekawa USA, Inc. will walk through and inspect the refrigeration system it installed, give follow-up training and make recommendations so the system works correctly. Work runs from June 23 to December 31, 2022, for up to $7,805.

output.headline: Pays King Construction Inspection up to $47,388 for state-required inspections at Melrose Leadership Academy
output.summary: King Construction Inspection, Inc. will provide the inspector of record services required by the Division of the State Architect for the Living Schoolyard Project at Melrose Leadership Academy at Maxwell Park. The not-to-exceed amount includes up to $4,308 for additional (contingency) services. Work runs from June 23 to October 28, 2022.

output.headline: Pays Construction Testing Services up to $36,321 for materials testing at Melrose Leadership Academy
output.summary: Construction Testing Services, Inc. will provide materials testing and special construction inspections required by the Division of the State Architect for the Living Schoolyard Project at Melrose Leadership Academy at Maxwell Park. The not-to-exceed amount includes up to $3,268.80 for additional (contingency) services. Work runs from June 23 to October 28, 2022.

output.headline: Agreement with Alameda County Health Care Services Agency for school health centers, up to $1.5M
output.summary: The board approves a services agreement under which the Alameda County Health Care Services Agency contracts with the district's school-based health centers to provide physical care and mental health services. It also covers the district's Central Family Resource Center for health-related and other services. The agreement is capped at $1,500,000.00 and covers July 1, 2021 through June 30, 2022, a period that began before the board's vote.

vendor.name: Alameda County Health Care Services Agency

It makes sure Measure N (College and Career Readiness for All Act) revenues are spent as the measure requires. It also sets out each party's operating and reporting duties.

output.headline: Pays School Facility Consultants up to $190,000 to pursue state and federal facilities funding
output.summary: School Facility Consultants will help the district pursue state and federal money for school buildings, including preparing funding applications and updating the district's eligibility for modernization and new construction. The not-to-exceed amount is $190,000 for work from July 1, 2022 to June 30, 2023.

output.headline: Ratifies $1,000 for Zymbolic to train educators in social and emotional learning for summer programs
output.summary: The board ratifies a services agreement with Zymbolic, LLC to provide professional learning for educators on Transformative Social and Emotional Learning for summer programming. The work is through the High School Linked Learning Office, runs June 1 through June 30, 2022, and is capped at $1,000.00.

output.headline: Approves $12.17M in Measure N college and career plans and budgets for district and charter high schools
output.summary: The board adopts a resolution, on the Measure N Commission's recommendation, approving 2022-2023 education improvement plans and budgets for district and charter high schools. This includes the Measure N administrative 10%. The total is $12,169,283.67 in Measure N (College and Career Readiness for All Act) funds.

output.headline: Adds $2.5M to Maxim Healthcare's COVID testing and contact tracing contract, raising it to $4.6M
output.sourceIssueCandidate: The title names Maxim Healthcare Staffing Services, Inc. while the text names Maxim Healthcare Services, Inc., and $2,100,000 of the added amount is described as a correction to Amendment No. 1.
output.summary: The board approves COVID-19 Addendum No. 2 to the district's master contract with Maxim Healthcare Services, Inc. for additional COVID testing and contact tracing personnel for July 1, 2021 through June 30, 2022. The $2,500,000 added is described as $2,100,000 correcting Amendment No. 1 plus $400,000 for Amendment No. 2. It raises the contract cap from $2,100,000.00 to $4,600,000.00, handled through the Programs for Exceptional Children Department.

output.headline: Aligns district COVID policies and practices with state and county public health guidance
output.summary: The board adopts a resolution to align the district's COVID policies, protocols and practices with state and county public health guidance. No dollar amount is stated.

output.headline: Lets unspent 2020-21 Measure G1 funds carry over and approves spending plans for named middle schools
output.summary: The board adopts a resolution, on the recommendation of the Measure G1 oversight commission, that permits carrying over unspent 2020-2021 Measure G1 (Teacher Retention and Middle School Improvement Act) funds into the 2021-2022 school year. It also approves spending plans for the named district and charter middle schools. No dollar amount is stated.

output.headline: Amends the 2021-22 Measure G1 middle school grant awards and spending plans
output.summary: The Board adopts a resolution recommended by the Measure G1 oversight commission that amends the 2021-22 grant application and education spending plan for district middle schools. Measure G1 is the local tax measure for teacher retention and middle school improvement. The official text does not state dollar amounts, schools or what changed.

output.headline: Adopts the 2022-23 Measure G1 middle school grant awards and spending plans
output.summary: The Board adopts a resolution recommended by the Measure G1 oversight commission for the 2022-23 grant application and education spending plan for district middle schools. Measure G1 is the local tax measure for teacher retention and middle school improvement. The official text does not state dollar amounts or which schools receive awards.

output.headline: Pays up to $75,846.87 for 2022-23 blanket accident insurance covering all enrolled students
output.summary: The board approves the application and payment for the district's Blanket Student Accident Insurance for fiscal year 2022-2023. The policy is underwritten by ACE American Insurance Company, and payment goes to the broker, Myers-Stevens & Toohey & Company, Inc. It covers all enrolled students for injuries on campus, at school-sponsored activities and on direct trips to and from school, up to $75,846.87.

output.headline: Pays up to $54,001.48 for 2022-23 catastrophic accident insurance for students and volunteers

money.evidence: not to exceed a cumulative cost of $54,001.48

output.sourceIssueCandidate: The title says Fiscal Year 2021-2022 while the text says 2022-2023, and the printed Coverage II cost ($43,533.16) does not equal 34,566 participants x $1.26, so the two listed costs do not add up to the stated $54,001.48 cap.
output.summary: The board approves the 2022-2023 coverage request and payment for catastrophic accident insurance for students and volunteers, underwritten by ACE American Insurance Company and paid through the broker Myers-Stevens & Toohey & Company, Inc. It has two parts: one for interscholastic athletics and one for other school activities. Total cost is capped at $54,001.48.

output.headline: Pays $3.5M for excess property and liability coverage and $967,000 for excess workers' comp coverage
output.summary: The board approves 2022-23 membership payments for two kinds of excess insurance. The larger is $3,502,288.00 for excess property and liability coverage through Northern California ReLiEF JPA (a joint powers authority, meaning a public agency pool), with Keenan & Associates as broker. The other is $967,000.00 for excess workers' compensation coverage through Public Risk Innovation, Solutions, and Management (PRISIM), with Alliant Insurance Services, Inc. as broker.

output.headline: Pays Arcina Risk Group up to $25,000 for insurance archaeology and claims advocacy
output.summary: The board approves a short services agreement with Arcina Risk Group, LLC for insurance archaeology (searching for past insurance coverage) and claims advocacy, for up to $25,000.00. The work runs from July 1, 2022 through October 1, 2022 and is handled through the Risk Management Department.

output.headline: Finds Yu Ming Charter School cannot be housed at one site and directs final Proposition 39 facilities offers
output.summary: The board adopts a resolution finding that Yu Ming Charter School cannot be accommodated at a single site and giving its written reasoning. It adopts the issuance of Proposition 39 facilities offers for the 2022-2023 school year (Proposition 39 covers sharing public school facilities with charter schools). It also directs staff to issue written final offers as that law requires.

output.headline: Ratifies two board president appointments to the Measure G1 teacher retention oversight commission
output.summary: The board ratifies the board president's appointments of Edmund Chun and Shivani Grover to the Measure G1 Districtwide Teacher Retention and Middle School Improvement Act Oversight Commission. Both are first-term appointments, effective June 23, 2022, with terms ending April 15, 2024.
